title: Appraisal Desk Note: Appraisal Age and the Successor Evidence Window in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Age of the appraisal.** For a successor's declaration on a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case, the age of the case's as-is appraisal is the number of whole calendar months from the appraisal date to the declaration date. An appraisal dated after the declaration date counts as less than 4 months old.

**Rule.**

- Where the case has no appraisal recorded, 21 calendar days are added to the evidence window.
- Where the appraisal is at least the plan's appraisal validity in months old (6 months under every plan), 14 calendar days are added.
- Where it is at least 4 and less than 6 months old, 7 calendar days are added.
- Where it is less than 4 months old, nothing is added.

| Appraisal on the case at the declaration date | Days added to the evidence window |
|---|---|
| none recorded | 21 |
| 6 whole months or older | 14 |
| 4 or 5 whole months | 7 |
| under 4 whole months, or dated after the declaration | 0 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical; declaration on 20 April)

- An appraisal dated 21 December is 3 whole months old, so nothing is added.
- An appraisal dated 20 December is 4 whole months old, so 7 days are added.
- An appraisal dated 20 October is 6 whole months old, so 14 days are added.
